themes.title: Excessive Advertising
themes.description: A large share of dissatisfied users cite frequent and intrusive ads as a major pain point. The ads interrupt listening sessions, appear after every few songs, and are perceived as a forced upsell to premium. This frustration drives churn among free-tier listeners.
quotes: plz block this app too many ads
Too many ADs and not enough skips.
themes.actionItem: Introduce a limited‑ads free tier (e.g., 3‑minute ad cap per hour) and clearly communicate the value of premium removal.

themes.title: Premium Cost Concerns
themes.description: Many reviewers feel the subscription price is too high and the price hikes are not justified. Users mention unexpected price increases and compare the cost unfavorably to the perceived value, especially when core features are locked behind the paywall.
quotes: Just got an email saying premium prices is going up to $12.99 and I'm just gonna delete my account entirely.
No reason to raise ur price
themes.actionItem: Offer flexible pricing options such as a lower‑cost tier with limited skips or a family plan discount to reduce price sensitivity.

themes.title: Playback & Stability Issues
themes.description: Technical glitches—including random app crashes, offline mode failures, and stuttering playback—are repeatedly reported. These problems affect both free and premium users, undermining trust in the platform's reliability.
quotes: The app keeps closing randomly when I'm running it on background.
It keeps stating that I'm offline initially after launching the app.
themes.actionItem: Prioritize a stability sprint to fix offline detection, reduce background crashes, and optimize playback buffering across devices.

report:
Executive Summary

Overall, Spotify remains a beloved music platform with a strong base of satisfied users, but three critical pain points are eroding the experience for a sizable minority. 

1. Excessive Advertising – Free‑tier listeners are repeatedly interrupted by ads, often after every few songs, leading to frustration and a perception that the service is pushing users toward paid plans. Evidence includes comments like "plz block this app too many ads" and "Too many ADs and not enough skips." Reducing ad frequency or offering a capped‑ads tier would address this.

2. Premium Cost Concerns – Price hikes and the high baseline subscription fee are viewed as unjustified, especially when core features feel locked. Users wrote, "Just got an email saying premium prices is going up to $12.99..." and "No reason to raise ur price." Introducing tiered pricing or discounted family plans could soften this backlash.

3. Playback & Stability Issues – Technical instability, such as random crashes and offline mode errors, appears in many negative reviews. Sample feedback: "The app keeps closing randomly when I'm running it on background" and "It keeps stating that I'm offline initially after launching the app." A focused stability sprint is needed.

Next Steps:
- Launch a limited‑ads free tier and communicate its benefits.
- Test and roll out a lower‑cost subscription option with partial premium features.
- Allocate engineering resources to resolve offline detection bugs and improve background stability.

Sentiment is currently tilted positive (53% satisfied), but the identified themes explain the 27% negative sentiment and highlight clear opportunities to improve retention and user happiness.
